image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) swimming in rippled water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow bill, a brown chest, and a grey/white body. It is floating on the surface with its body partially submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and bright yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible as a small, dark spot on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant. The plumage texture appears dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, brown chest, and greyish flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged underwater and not visible in this image.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body, appearing broad and structurally sound.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers typical of mallard drakes.
